scenes.headline: How a System One model decides without writing
scenes.sub: Jev: typed questions in, one forward pass, a probability for every option.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Sprinkles! Jev is a new kind of model that makes decisions without writing a word. Here's how it works.

scenes.text: Jev reads the answer instead of writing it: typed questions in, a probability for every option out, from one forward pass.
scenes.mark: reads the answer instead of writing it
scenes.say: Here's the idea: read the answer instead of writing it. Typed questions go in, and one forward pass gives a probability for every option.

scenes.title: Two ways to make a decision

left.title: An LLM call
items: Samples a token, appends it, repeats
Spells out JSON for your code to parse
left.say: An LLM decision call samples a token, appends it, and repeats, until it has spelled out JSON your code must parse.

right.title: Jev
items: Reads option logits in one pass
Can only pick an option you gave
right.say: Jev skips the loop. It reads the answer instead of writing it, so it can't return a malformed one, though it can still be confidently wrong.

scenes.title: One call, every question at once

steps.say: You send a state and typed questions: a Choice among up to two hundred and fifty-five options, a Score on a rubric, or a yes-no Noul.
One forward pass reads every option's logit directly, and returns a full distribution for each question, all in parallel. Nothing is decoded.

steps.note: type-safe by construction, not correct by construction
steps.say: Your code takes it from there. Jev is a smart if statement, and it can only answer with an option you supplied.
Because every answer carries a confidence, you can route just the unsure ones to a bigger model.

scenes.title: Same 4B model, same 21 questions
scenes.note: openjev, one RTX 3090, median of 3 runs
scenes.say: Hold the model fixed and switch only the readout. Reading logits took about one second; generating the JSON took five point three. That's the honest size of the trick.

scenes.text: The speed is the architecture, which outsiders rebuilt within days. Calibrated training is plausibly the hard part, and it's undisclosed.

recap: Typed questions in, distributions out, one pass
Reading logits beat generating JSON by 5.21x
Type-safe by construction; calibration still unpublished
scenes.say: To recap: typed questions, one pass, logits read not written, and a calibration story still waiting for its evidence.
